assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2018 observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states at the magic angle in twisted bilayer graphene opened an entirely new field of moire quantum matter. The discovery is clear and nature-led, a surprise confirmed by experiment, and it was preceded by a sharp theoretical prediction of flat bands at a specific angle. Impact on condensed matter is broad and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 continuum-model prediction of the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 experimental discovery. This theory plus experiment trio is a natural prize configuration. The first-author experimentalist Yuan Cao is not in the credited names, and other groups (for example Dean, Young, Yazdani) contributed to the follow-up, so credit is not perfectly clean.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced by many groups across several platforms within a few years, and the physical interpretation is still developing but the core observations are robust. Recognition in 2026 would be early but defensible given the rapid confirmation.
uncertainties: Whether the mechanism of superconductivity in the magic-angle system is settled is unclear to me and I have not verified the current state of the field.
Early-career contributors such as Yuan Cao fall outside the credited names, which limits fair allocation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos in 2013, the 2018 association with the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the 2022 identification of NGC 1068 and the Galactic plane constitute the opening of a new observational window. This is a discovery at the centre, in the sense of a genuinely new observation of nature, and a flagship of multimessenger astronomy.
assessment.attribution: IceCube was a large collaboration and credit is spread widely. Halzen is the originator and long-time leader of the concept and the principal investigator; Spiering is a senior figure in the collaboration and in neutrino astronomy. Other names who led construction and analysis (for instance Gaisser, Karle, Kowalski) are absent from the credited list, so a two-person prize would leave out significant contributors, and I cannot independently settle the allocation.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent confirmations in the 2018 and 2022 results and a stable interpretation of a diffuse astrophysical flux, though source populations remain incompletely understood. Timing seems ripe.
uncertainties: The IceCube collaboration is large and the supplied names may not capture the decisive individuals.
Source-class identification remains partial; sources of most of the diffuse flux are unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The BB84 protocol and Ekert's entanglement-based protocol founded quantum cryptography, with security grounded in the laws of quantum mechanics rather than computational assumptions. The impact is conceptual and technological, and the work is deeply tied to foundations of quantum theory, including Bell nonlocality, which the Committee recognised in 2022.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard are the clear originators of BB84 and Ekert independently proposed the E91 protocol with entanglement; this makes a natural three-person prize. The list contains two spellings of Ekert; I use the plain form as one person. Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is not credited and is deceased, which is a minor historical wrinkle.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: decades of experiments, satellite and fibre demonstrations and commercial systems, and the theory is understood. Practical device-security issues do not diminish the foundational discovery.
uncertainties: Whether the Committee views this as physics discovery versus information-science invention, I cannot resolve.
The relation of BB84 to Wiesner's earlier unpublished idea may affect credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological insulator, followed by the experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells, launched the field of time-reversal-invariant topological matter. The concept is original, the experimental confirmation is concrete, and the impact on materials and quantum transport is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical proposals; Molenkamp's group delivered the 2007 experimental observation following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. Shoucheng Zhang, a key contributor, is deceased, and Bernevig and Hughes are not in the credited names, so the allocation is a compromise and not obviously complete. Three-person configuration is available.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by ARPES observations in Bi-based materials and by transport; the interpretation is stable. The 2016 prize on topological phase transitions covers related but distinct ground, so this is timely but follows recent recognition of the field.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2016 prize may reduce the Committee's appetite.
Zhang's death and omission of Bernevig and Hughes complicate fairness.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, based on Katori's magic-wavelength concept, reached fractional uncertainties near 10^-18 and enable tests of fundamental constants, relativistic time dilation at centimetre scales and a path to redefinition of the second. Clear, quantifiable and a precision-measurement achievement with large downstream value.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice clock and Ye drove the experimental performance to the 10^-18 regime with strontium; a two-person prize is natural. Hall and Hansch were already recognised for the frequency comb, which underlies the work, and Ludlow and others contributed, so the boundary of credit is somewhat subjective.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by several laboratories worldwide with consistent record accuracy; mature. Redefinition of the SI second is still pending, which may affect timing.
uncertainties: Whether the Committee regards this as sufficiently distinct from the 2005 frequency comb prize.
Other trapped-ion clock contributors (Wineland-linked groups) are not in the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of neutron stars with magnetic fields of 10^14 to 10^15 G and their identification with soft gamma repeaters and anomalous X-ray pulsars explain a distinct class of compact objects and the giant flares. This is a clean case of a prediction confirmed by observation, with relevance to extreme matter and electrodynamics.
assessment.attribution: Duncan and Thompson made the 1992 theoretical prediction and Kouveliotou's 1998 discovery of the slow spin-down and period measurement of SGR 1806-20 supplied the observational confirmation. This theory and observation division gives a coherent three-person prize. Paczynski, a related early proponent, is deceased and uncredited.
assessment.maturity: Well established by many sources and the 2004 giant flare, and in more recent years the connection to fast radio bursts through SGR 1935+2154 adds a new relevance. Mature but not urgent.
uncertainties: Attribution of the very first magnetar proposal versus the Duncan-Thompson model is somewhat contested, as I recall.
Some details of the observational confirmation chronology I have not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise Hubbard-type models with exquisite control, enabling the observation of the superfluid to Mott insulator transition and later quantum gas microscopy, and thereby quantum simulation of strongly correlated matter. The idea is original and the technique is widely adopted.
assessment.attribution: Five names are credited, and the decisive allocation is ambiguous. Zoller and Jaksch proposed the Hubbard realisation, Greiner and Bloch observed the Mott transition and developed microscopy, Esslinger realised fermionic Mott insulators, and Cirac shares theoretical credit. I chose Bloch, Greiner and Zoller as a defensible configuration, but this is subjective.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and replicated across laboratories. Whether it is a discovery of a new phenomenon or a powerful technique is arguable, and the simulation of materially unsolved problems is still maturing.
uncertainties: The prize configuration is contested among five principal contributors.
Quantum simulation has not yet resolved a major open question, to my knowledge.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Event Horizon Telescope delivered the first horizon-scale images of the shadow of M87* and Sgr A*, a direct visual test of strong-field general relativity and the existence of black holes. Compelling and widely understood, and of obvious interest from a gravitational physics perspective.
assessment.attribution: The EHT is a very large collaboration and the three credited names cover the concept (Falcke's shadow proposal), the leadership of the array (Doeleman) and the VLBI development (Moran), but many others (for example the theory and imaging teams) are not included. The Nobel rule of three makes attribution awkward.
assessment.maturity: Two independent sources imaged with consistent size matching general relativity. Interpretation of the image, including spin and jet launching, still has open questions, and the 2020 prize already recognised black-hole physics. Timeliness is moderate.
uncertainties: Collaboration size makes a fair three-person allocation difficult.
The scientific novelty relative to existing black-hole evidence (LIGO, stellar orbits at Sgr A*) may be seen as incremental.
